native_result.query: What kind of demographic disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated?
native_result.HypoA: Gender disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated, with males having higher median wealth than females.
native_result.HypoB: Among NLSY79 respondents who were ever incarcerated (ever_jailed=1, jailed sometime in 1985-1994), 1985 wealth is sharply demographically stratified. The most robust disparity is racial, among men: white men held a median of $2,000 (n=57), roughly 2.5x the Black-male median ($800, n=143; gap -$1,200) and ~2.9x the Hispanic-male median ($700, n=52; gap -$1,300). The starkest disparity is by sex within minority groups: Black and Hispanic women who were ever incarcerated had median wealth of $0 - an absence of assets rather than debts (0% negative values among Black women) - with 78-81% reporting exactly zero wealth, versus $700-$800 for same-race men. White women (n=12) show the numerically highest median ($4,100, +$2,100 vs white men), but this small cell is not headline material. As background contrast, the pooled ever-incarcerated median ($720, n=289) sits far below the never-incarcerated median ($3,600, n=11,724). Caveats: ever_jailed spans 1985-1994, so 1985 wealth may predate or postdate incarceration for part of the group - the pattern is a descriptive association, not causal; 5.4% of 1985 wealth values are negative (net debts) and 26.7% are exactly zero, so medians near zero partly reflect the mass at zero; medians are not fully stable to full-row deduplication (shifts up to $1,300, narrowing the Hispanic-male deficit), and small female cells (n=9-16) make within-race sex gaps suggestive rather than definitive.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 rows, 6 cols, 0 missing; race value typo 'hipanic' kept as-is in data, reported as Hispanic in prose). Diagnostics: composite_wealth_1985 spans -$57,587 to $2,574,706 with 649 negatives (5.4%, net-of-debt composite) and 3,209 zeros (26.7%); 2,056 rows in 157 exact-duplicate groups (largest 617 rows), retained in main analysis with dedup sensitivity rerun; no residence or timing columns exist, so the residence-based incarceration proxy could not be applied and ever_jailed (binary, 289 ever = 2.4%) was taken at face value. Main analysis: ever_jailed=1 subset grouped by race x sex; median/mean/zero-share/neg-share per cell; dollar gaps and ratios vs reference white male; full 15-pair pairwise comparisons with ratios only where reference median > $0. Background: same breakdown for ever_jailed=0. Sensitivity: full-row dedup shifts medians up to $1,300 (black male 800->1,400, hipanic male 700->2,000, white male 2,000->2,100; female zero-medians unchanged). Conclusions ordered: male race gaps first, then sex-within-race, then small-cell and zero-median caveats; conclusions resting on n<15 not headlined.

sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 white respondents with ever_jailed=1 during 1985–1994; the white-female cell contains only 12 respondents.
sub_hypo.relations: White women's median wealth was $2,100 higher than white men's $2,000 median. The small-cell association is suggestive rather than definitive and is not causal.

sub_hypo.text: The pooled ever-incarcerated group had median 1985 wealth of $720 (n=289), far below the never-incarcerated group's $3,600 (n=11,724).
sub_hypo.context: Full NLSY79 analysis dataset; ever_jailed distinguishes respondents jailed sometime in 1985–1994 from those not jailed during that interval.
sub_hypo.relations: Ever-incarcerated respondents had substantially lower median 1985 wealth than never-incarcerated respondents. This background contrast is descriptive, not causal, because incarceration timing relative to 1985 wealth is unavailable.

sub_hypo.text: In the full dataset, 5.4% of 1985 wealth values were negative and 26.7% were exactly zero, so medians near zero partly reflect the concentration of observations at zero.
sub_hypo.context: Full NLSY79 analysis dataset of 12,013 rows, with exact duplicates retained.
sub_hypo.relations: The wealth distribution includes negative values representing net debts and a substantial mass at exactly zero, qualifying the interpretation of near-zero medians.
